story_text.value:
I saw this LinkedIn post from a Meta engineer and it resonated with me:

https://www.linkedin.com/posts/ali-hamie_im-an-engineer-at-m...

> I'm an engineer at Meta and I never felt this uncomfortable doing my job. I'm writing code these days and it all feels like a black box. This new standard of shipping with AI is moving so fast that if we're going to spend our time checking each line of code, it's going to take forever. That means you can end up with systems you've built where you don't truly understand how all the code works. You understand the high level, but not every detail. And maybe this is becoming the new standard. It goes against every instinct of being a software engineer. I'm used to understanding what I'm building. Now I'm trying to figure out how much I need to understand before I'm comfortable moving forward. Are other engineers feeling this too?

How are you handling this?

title.value: Ask HN: How to deal with shipping AI-written code you don't understand?

story_text.value:
Hello HN,

This is Diego from Krea. Today we are announcing the open beta of Krea 3, our newest foundational image model.

In a nutshell, it’s a frontier image model in terms of quality, but at a fraction of the speed and a fraction of the price.

We will be releasing a more technical update, like we did with Krea 2 (https://www.krea.ai/blog/krea-2-technical-report), but this website shows the capabilities we focused on:

* Native regional edits

* Precise edits so that there is minimal area degradation pixel-wise

* Frontier image quality. Benchmarks still being worked on, but in our internal evals it seems a no-brainer replacement to NBP or GPT Image, both speed and cost-wise.

* Faster edits (AFAICK, this should unlock a pareto frontier for speed in frontier edit models).

In terms of future updates, the team is thinking about letting folks fine-tune Krea 3 (via LoRAs) and open-weights, but we’re still in the middle of launch hiccups and then we’ll revisit the next iterations.

Thanks!

title.value: Krea 3 – An image model built for editing at scale
